svg.title: E8 orbit memory
svg.desc: Three parts. Left: the 240 E8 roots drawn as a ring of 15 clusters of 16, the orbits. A query half snaps to its nearest root, found in 8 operations rather than a 240-way scan, and the other 15 members of that root's orbit light up as candidates. Right: a 240 by 240 grid of 57,600 value slots where the candidate roots of two halves cross and the top 8 cells light up and are read from a value table of about 59 megabytes per layer, beside a dense layer drawn as a full block that costs about 270 thousand multiply-adds per token against about 27 thousand (design arithmetic, not measured). Bottom: held-out bits per byte, lower is better: dense 1.4078, learned keys 1.4175, E8 on half the layers 1.4406, E8 on all eight layers 1.5237, with the 0.0054 noise marked. The learned keys beat the E8 half by 0.0231, about four times the noise.
svg.text: E8 orbit memory: a few rows read by address instead of a dense layer
1 Snap to a root, read its orbit
Schematic ring: placement is not the E8 geometry.

top k = 8 cells (k = 8 in the rung)
3 Held-out bits per byte (lower is better)

text.tspan: learned keys lead by 0.0231, about 4 × noise
